metadata.title: On the Distribution of the Length of the Longest Increasing Subsequence of Random Permutations (Baik, Deift, Johansson, 1999)
metadata.framework: Asymptotic distribution of the longest increasing subsequence length via Riemann-Hilbert steepest descent and determinantal formulas
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:math/9810105.

nodes.name: Longest increasing subsequence
nodes.statement: For a random permutation $\pi \in S_n$ (uniform distribution), let $\ell_n = \ell_n(\pi)$ denote the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $\pi$, i.e., the largest $k$ such that there exist $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ with $\pi(i_1) < \pi(i_2) < \cdots < \pi(i_k)$.

nodes.name: Tracy-Widom distribution $F_2$
nodes.statement: The Tracy-Widom distribution $F_2$ is the limiting distribution of the largest eigenvalue of a GUE (Gaussian Unitary Ensemble) random matrix, appropriately centered and scaled. It is expressed as $F_2(t) = \exp\left(-\int_t^\infty (s - t) q(s)^2 \, ds\right)$, where $q(s)$ is the Hastings-McLeod solution of the Painleve II equation $q'' = sq + 2q^3$, with $q(s) \sim \mathrm{Ai}(s)$ as $s \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Poissonization
nodes.statement: Instead of studying $\ell_n$ directly, the problem is Poissonized: consider $N \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$ points uniformly distributed in $[0,1]^2$, and let $\ell(\lambda)$ be the length of the longest up-right path. The distribution of $\ell(\lambda)$ is related to $\ell_n$ through de-Poissonization lemmas. The Poissonized problem has a determinantal structure.

nodes.name: Determinantal formula (Gessel identity)
nodes.statement: By the RSK correspondence, $\Pr(\ell(\lambda) \le k) = e^{-\lambda} \det(I - K)_{L^2(k, k+1, \ldots)}$, where $K$ is an integral operator related to Bessel functions. This reduces the distributional problem to the asymptotic analysis of a Fredholm determinant, which is the starting point for Riemann-Hilbert analysis.

nodes.name: Riemann-Hilbert steepest descent method
nodes.statement: The Fredholm determinant is analyzed via the Deift-Zhou steepest descent method for Riemann-Hilbert problems. The orthogonal polynomial kernel defining $K$ is expressed as the solution of a $2 \times 2$ matrix RH problem, which is then asymptotically solved through a sequence of explicit transformations (normalization, opening of lenses, parametrix construction near the edge) that reduce the problem to a local Airy parametrix at the soft edge.

nodes.name: BDJ theorem: Tracy-Widom limit for longest increasing subsequence
nodes.statement: As $n \to \infty$, $\Pr\left(\frac{\ell_n - 2\sqrt{n}}{n^{1/6}} \le t\right) \to F_2(t)$, where $F_2$ is the Tracy-Widom distribution for GUE. That is, the centered and scaled length of the longest increasing subsequence of a random permutation converges in distribution to the same limit as the largest eigenvalue of a GUE matrix.
conclusions: Connection between combinatorics (permutations) and random matrix theory (GUE)

nodes.name: Moment convergence
nodes.statement: All moments of the rescaled variable $\frac{\ell_n - 2\sqrt{n}}{n^{1/6}}$ converge to the corresponding moments of the Tracy-Widom distribution $F_2$. This strengthens distributional convergence to moment convergence.

nodes.name: Vershik-Kerov and Logan-Shepp limit
nodes.statement: It was previously known (Vershik-Kerov 1977, Logan-Shepp 1977) that $\ell_n / \sqrt{n} \to 2$ in probability. The BDJ theorem provides the next-order refinement: the fluctuations around $2\sqrt{n}$ are of order $n^{1/6}$ and follow the Tracy-Widom law.

edges.note: The LIS problem is Poissonized for analysis.
The determinantal formula is analyzed via Riemann-Hilbert methods.
Steepest descent asymptotics yield the Tracy-Widom limit.
The Tracy-Widom distribution is the limiting law.
Moment convergence strengthens the distributional result.
